summary: Builds the daily production schedule for each line based on open orders, machine availability, and material readiness.
Lets planners simulate the impact of adding a rush order to the schedule before committing, showing which other orders would slip.
Sequences production runs to minimize costly changeover time between product variants on a shared line.
Orders confirmed customer orders into a production sequence that respects due dates and priority tiers.
Gives an outgoing shift supervisor a structured way to log open issues and schedule status for the incoming shift.
Captures inline inspection measurements as parts move through the line and flags any reading outside the specified tolerance.
Lets a line inspector log a defect with photos and a defect code, routing it to the responsible station for root-cause review.
Charts statistical process control data for key measurements, alerting quality engineers when a process trends out of control.
Defines and enforces the inspection sampling plan for each product, ensuring the right number of units are checked per batch.
Scores incoming supplier lots on defect rate and tracks trends per supplier to inform sourcing decisions.
Manages maintenance work orders from creation through completion, prioritizing requests that affect a currently running line.
Tracks spare parts inventory for critical equipment and alerts the maintenance team before a commonly needed part runs out.
Logs the cause and duration of every unplanned line stoppage, feeding a downtime report reviewed at the daily production meeting.
Schedules recurring preventive maintenance tasks for each piece of equipment and blocks the affected line's production calendar accordingly.
Assigns the nearest available maintenance technician to a reported equipment fault and tracks response time against the plant's SLA.
Runs material requirements planning against the production schedule to generate purchase and work order recommendations.
Tracks actual supplier lead times against quoted lead times, adjusting planning buffers for suppliers trending slower than promised.
Recommends safety stock levels for each component based on demand variability and supplier reliability.
Combines sales forecasts, open orders, and historical demand into a single signal used to drive material planning.
Balances component allocation across multiple plants producing the same product family when total supply is constrained.
Tracks raw material lots from receiving through consumption on the line, keeping a live count of on-hand quantities.
Assembles the exact set of components a work order needs into a kit before it reaches the line, reducing line-side search time.
Guides warehouse staff through scheduled cycle counts on a handheld scanner and reconciles variances against the inventory system.
Traces a finished unit back to the exact raw material lots used in it, supporting rapid recall scoping if a defect is found.
Lets line operators log scrapped material with a reason code, rolling up into a scrap rate report reviewed weekly by plant leadership.
Shows a live board of every machine's current state, running, idle, or down, across the shop floor for supervisors to scan at a glance.
Calculates overall equipment effectiveness for each line from availability, performance, and quality data pulled off the machines.
Lets an operator trigger an andon alert when a line issue needs supervisor attention, logging response time until it's resolved.
Measures actual cycle time per unit at each station and flags stations running slower than the standard time.
Gives a machine operator a simple touchscreen to log production counts, downtime reasons, and quality checks during their shift.
Lets any employee report a workplace safety incident with details and photos, routing it to the safety team for investigation.
Logs near-miss safety events separately from actual incidents, helping the safety team spot hazards before they cause an injury.
Lets floor supervisors log spot checks of personal protective equipment compliance across shifts and departments.
Guides a safety auditor through a standardized plant walkthrough checklist and tracks corrective actions to completion.
Tracks which safety certifications each employee holds and flags upcoming expirations before they lapse.
Walks a new hire through a structured onboarding path of safety and role-specific training before they're cleared for the floor.
Tracks equipment operation certifications earned by each worker and blocks scheduling them on machines they're not certified for.
Shows a supervisor a visual matrix of which workers are trained on which stations, helping plan coverage for absences.
Delivers short, focused training modules to a worker's handheld device on a new procedure before their next shift.
Schedules cross-training sessions to broaden the plant's certified workforce and reduce single points of failure on key stations.
Gives suppliers a self-service portal to view open purchase orders, submit shipment confirmations, and update lead times.
Publishes a supplier's on-time delivery and quality scorecard so both sides can track performance against agreed targets.
Lets suppliers acknowledge or propose changes to a purchase order's quantity and date directly through the portal.
Logs a quality issue found in an incoming supplier shipment and tracks the supplier's corrective action response to resolution.
Lets a supplier commit to production capacity for upcoming periods, giving planners advance visibility into potential constraints.
Analyzes vibration sensor data from rotating equipment to detect early signs of bearing wear before a failure occurs.
Scores critical assets on likelihood of failure in the coming weeks, letting maintenance prioritize which units to inspect first.
Watches the condition monitoring sensors themselves, flagging ones reporting flat or erratic data that need recalibration.
Recommends the specific maintenance action to take on an asset flagged as at-risk, based on the sensor pattern that triggered the alert.
Tracks an asset's full maintenance and repair history against its expected service life to inform replacement budgeting.
Sends the correct label template and variable data to the packaging line's printer for each product and destination combination.
Determines the optimal carton size and unit count per case for a given product, minimizing wasted space and material cost.
Validates that a product's packaging label meets destination-market regulatory requirements before the run is approved.
Generates a pallet manifest listing every case and lot loaded onto a pallet as it's built at the end of the packaging line.
Assigns and tracks unique serial numbers on regulated products through packaging, supporting track-and-trace compliance requirements.
Shows plant leadership a daily rollup of throughput, quality, and downtime KPIs across every line in the facility.
Tracks energy consumption per line and per unit produced, helping identify equipment running inefficiently during off-shifts.
Analyzes first-pass yield by line and shift, helping engineers isolate which process step is driving the most rework or scrap.
Calculates the fully loaded cost per unit produced on each line, incorporating labor, material, and overhead allocations.
Compares KPIs for the same product line running at multiple plants, surfacing best practices from the top-performing site.
